stories.title: World Series Game 3 — Freddy Peralta Faces His Former Team TONIGHT
stories.angle: Game 3 of the 2026 World Series is TONIGHT at 8 PM ET at Tropicana Field (FOX). Brewers lead 2-0. The headline is Freddy Peralta — who spent all eight of his MLB seasons in Milwaukee — now starting for the Rays, trying to keep Tampa Bay alive against his former team. Peralta was traded to the Mets in January 2026, then acquired by Tampa Bay at the deadline. He's been dominant: 2-0, 1.08 ERA, 12 strikeouts this postseason; his Rays went 9-0 in his last 9 regular-season starts. Robert Gasser starts for Milwaukee (1.00 ERA in 9 postseason innings, including a 5-inning shutout in NLCS G3 vs. Dodgers). First World Series game at Tropicana since 2008.

stories.title: Rays Down 2-0 — What History Says About Their Chances
stories.angle: Down 0-2 in the World Series, the Rays face steep odds: teams that go up 2-0 in the Fall Classic have won 77 of 92 series, roughly 84%. Only 10 times in World Series history has a team come back from 0-2 to win — and the most recent was the 1996 Yankees defeating the Braves in six games. But Tampa Bay has factors in their favor: Peralta starts G3 at home, Rasmussen is available, and the Rays are 3-1 at Tropicana this postseason. G3, G4, and G5 are all at home.

stories.title: Misiorowski's Record-Breaking Arm — The Stats Behind the Fastest Pitch in WS History
stories.angle: Jacob Misiorowski threw a 103.5 mph fastball in WS Game 1 — the fastest pitch in the tracking era of the World Series. He also set an MLB regular-season record with 1,115 pitches above 100 mph in 2026. But there's a catch: his four-seamer's whiff rate fell from 40.2% in the regular season to 16.1% in the playoffs, suggesting hitters have adjusted. He has yet to complete 5 innings in either postseason start. His arm is historic; his postseason results are a work in progress.

stories.title: William Contreras — The Most Entertaining Postseason Star You're Not Watching
stories.angle: William Contreras has become the unlikely star of Milwaukee's World Series run. Through the NLCS, he batted .367 with 3 home runs, 9-for-23 with a .481 OBP and 1.264 OPS. His slow home run trots have become the signature of the Brewers' postseason run. The contrast is striking: in his first 20 career postseason games before 2026, he batted .211 with a .639 OPS. Something clicked.

stories.title: First-Time Championship Chasers — Why This World Series Is Different
stories.angle: The 2026 World Series is the first Fall Classic since 1980 where both franchises have NEVER won a championship. The Brewers (founded 1969) and Rays (1998) have each made it to the World Series before but never won. That means one of these franchises — already the underdog in baseball's most celebrated event — will finally break through after decades of fans rooting for a title that always seemed just out of reach.
